And many of the Egyptians were killed,
and the rest fled in ships. And in the year
1039 [of the Greeks],
Maslama again invaded the land of the Turks,
and the Arabs were defeated,
and they abandoned their baggage and fled.
And in the year 1042 [of the Greeks],
the Turks {OCR: ܓܘܪ̈ܩܝܐ for ܛܘܪ̈ܩܝܐ?} went forth
and captured the cities of Azerbaijan.
And Maslama went against them with a large army,
and thousands and tens of thousands were killed on both sides.
Now the Turks, when they held the cities they had conquered,
did not advance against the rest of the Arabs' territory.
And the Arabs made peace with the Turks.
And the Arabs entered the territory of the Romans again with Mu'awiya the son of the king (Caliph),
and they tore down the walls of the city of Gangra,
and they went and struck against the city of Nicaea.
And when they had fought for forty days and torn down its wall,
the Romans who were in it fled in ships.
And the Arabs captured it and destroyed it.
And Hisham gave orders,
and all the Roman prisoners were killed,
because he heard that Leo had killed the Arab prisoners.
And at this time, King Leo took the daughter of the Khagan, the king of the Khazars, as a wife for his son Constantine.
And when they had baptized her and blessed her,
he placed a crown upon his son,
and proclaimed him emperor.
In the year 1048 [of the Greeks],
a man whose name was Bashir,
who was of Roman descent,
and in appearance an Arab (Muslim),
went to Harran and entered into the presence of an apostate man whose name was Theophilus.
And as if in secret he revealed to him
that he was allegedly Tiberius, the son of Constantius (Constans,
Constantine) (perhaps Justinian?), the one who was thought to have died long ago.
Then that Roman went and denounced him to Sulayman, the son of Hisham.
And the latter, having seized him, informed his father Hisham.
Then Hisham, rejoicing that the son of the king of the Romans had fallen into his hands,
ordered that they clothe {OCR: ܓܪܫܘܗܝ for ܓܠܣܘܗܝ/ܐܠܒܫܘܗܝ?} him in purple garments,
and bring him to him.
This man, when he entered Edessa, went into the sanctuary and received the Eucharist with his own hands from the table of life,
according to the custom of the Roman emperors.
And he summoned the Jews to raise for him [spirits] with necromancy {OCR?},
and also the head of the Harranians to examine the liver for him,
to see how his affair would turn out.
And in the end the wretched man was exposed,
and he was executed.
And in the year 1053 [of the Greeks],
